cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I only finished one painting for our exhibition. Tell me I've done enough. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice the gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I need to know I've contributed, not that you can hide where I haven't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours belongs in the middle. It's the one people will see first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce me as the other painter. No 'despite everything'. I want to hear that I belong here.

mechanism: A directs exhibition setup while accommodating B placement proposal to obtain reassurance that one completed painting is a sufficient contribution.
confusable: Unlike seeking inflated praise, A wants effort counted as enough; borrowed authority keeps arranging the show while relying on B to affirm A place in it.
comparison: One painting in a shared exhibition differs from finishing a difficult speech with an omitted paragraph.
seedUse: Use D100-a one painting/gap/middle/fellow painter and S02-a modifying the display plan around B reassuring participation.
